nodes.name: Minimal surface
nodes.statement: An immersed surface $X$ in a Riemannian manifold $M$ is called a \emph{minimal surface} if it is a critical point (or, what is equivalent in this case, a local minimizer) of the area under compact perturbations; think of a soap film.

nodes.name: Branched minimal surface
nodes.statement: We will use a slightly more general notion of a minimal surface that need only be immersed outside a set of isolated branch points (at which the surface can self-intersect locally), cf.\ \cite{GOR73}. These objects, called \emph{branched} minimal surfaces, arise naturally when taking limits of immersed minimal surfaces.

nodes.name: Bryant's theorem
nodes.statement: For example, a question in this spirit is: can an $N$-dimensional sphere---a manifold with constant \emph{positive} curvature---contain a minimal surface that has constant \emph{negative} curvature? It was shown by Bryant~\cite{Bry85} that the answer is no.

nodes.name: Song's theorem
nodes.statement: There exist closed minimal surfaces $X_j$ in Euclidean unit spheres $\mathbb{S}^{N_j}$ so that the Gaussian curvature $K_j$ of $X_j$ satisfies $$ \lim_{j\to\infty}\frac{1}{\mathrm{Area}(X_j)}\int_{X_j} |K_j+8| = 0. $$
conclusions: There exist closed minimal surfaces $X_j$ in Euclidean unit spheres $\mathbb{S}^{N_j}$
nodes.label: thm:song

nodes.name: Dirichlet energy
nodes.statement: If $f:X\to M$ is a map from a Riemann surface $X$ to a Riemannian manifold $M$, its Dirichlet energy is defined by $$ \mathrm{E}(f) = \frac{1}{2}\int_X |df|^2. $$

nodes.name: Harmonic map
nodes.statement: A critical point of the energy is called a \emph{harmonic map}.

nodes.name: Weakly conformal harmonic maps are minimal surfaces
nodes.statement: If $f$ is weakly conformal (i.e., conformal away from branch points), then $\mathrm{E}(f)$ coincides with the area of the surface $f(X)$ in $M$. Thus a weakly conformal map $f$ is harmonic if and only if $f(X)$ is a minimal surface in $M$.

nodes.name: Finite-range unitary representation setup
nodes.statement: Let us write $X=\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H}$, and consider a unitary representation $\pi_N:\Gamma\to U(N)$ with finite range $|\pi_N(\Gamma)|<\infty$ which we view as acting on the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{2N-1}$ of $\mathbb{C}^N$ with its standard Euclidean metric.

nodes.name: Song's equivariant energy minimization problem
nodes.statement: The following variational problem is considered in \cite{Son24}: $$ \mathrm{E}(X,\pi_N) = \inf\bigg\{ \frac{1}{2}\int_F |df|^2 ; ~ f:\mathbb{H}\to\mathbb{S}^{2N-1}\text{ is } \pi_N\text{-equivariant}\bigg\}, $$ where $F$ is the fundamental domain of the action of $\Gamma$ on $\mathbb{H}$.

nodes.name: Equivariant minimizers give symmetric minimal surfaces
nodes.statement: Since a minimizer $f_N$ in $\mathrm{E}(X,\pi_N)$ minimizes the Dirichlet energy, it defines\footnote{ Even though $X^N$ has punctures, taking the closure of $f_N(X^N)$ yields a closed surface. This is a nontrivial property of harmonic maps, see \cite[\S 4.6.4]{Moo17}.} a minimal surface $f_N(X^N)$ in $\mathbb{S}^{2N-1}$ that has many symmetries (it contains many rotated copies of the image $f_N(F)$ of the fundamental domain).

nodes.name: Subsequential limit of equivariant minimizers
nodes.statement: Once a minimizer $f_N$ has been chosen for every $N$, we can take $N\to\infty$ to obtain a limiting object. Indeed, if we embed each $\mathbb{S}^{2N-1}$ in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^\infty$ of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$, we can view all $f_N:\mathbb{H}\to\mathbb{S}^\infty$ on the same footing. Then the properties of harmonic maps furnish enough compactness to ensure that $f_N$ converges along a subsequence to a limiting map $f_\infty:\mathbb{H}\to\mathbb{S}^\infty$, which is $\pi_\infty$-equivariant for some unitary representation $\pi_\infty:\Gamma\to B(H)$.

nodes.name: Weak equivalence of unitary representations
nodes.statement: Here two unitary representations $\rho_1:\Gamma\to B(H_1)$ and $\rho_2:\Gamma\to B(H_2)$ are said to be \emph{weakly equivalent} if any matrix element of $\rho_1$ can be approximated uniformly on compacts by finite linear combinations of matrix elements of $\rho_2$, and vice versa.

nodes.name: Rigidity of equivariant energy minimizers
nodes.statement: Let $\rho:\Gamma\to B(H)$ be a unitary representation of $\Gamma$ that is weakly equivalent to the regular representation $\lambda_\Gamma$. Then any $\rho$-equivariant energy-minimizing map $\varphi:\mathbb{H}\to\mathbb{S}^\infty$ must satisfy $\varphi^*g_{\mathbb{S}^\infty} = \frac{1}{8}g_{\rm hyp}$, where $g_{\rm hyp}$ denotes the hyperbolic metric on $\mathbb{H}$ (so $\frac{1}{8}g_{\rm hyp}$ is the metric on $\mathbb{H}$ with constant curvature $-8$).
assumptions: Let $\rho:\Gamma\to B(H)$ be a unitary representation of $\Gamma$ that is weakly equivalent to the regular representation $\lambda_\Gamma$.
nodes.label: thm:songkey

nodes.name: Proof idea for Theorem 5.13
nodes.statement: The proof of this result is one of the main ingredients of \cite{Son24}. Very roughly speaking, one first produces a single $\rho$ and $\varphi$ that satisfy the conclusion of the theorem by an explicit construction; weak equivalence is then used to transfer the conclusion to other $\rho$ and $\varphi$ as in the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Explicit construction for one representation, then transfer by weak equivalence.

nodes.name: Weak equivalence of the limit forces curvature -8
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{thm:songkey} explains the utility of constructing equivariant minimal surfaces: if we choose the sequence of representations $\pi_N$ in such a way that the limiting representation $\pi_\infty$ is weakly equivalent to the regular representation, then this will automatically imply that the metrics $f_N^*g_{\mathbb{S}^{2N-1}}$ on the minimal surfaces converge to the metric $f_\infty^*g_{\mathbb{S}^\infty}=\frac{1}{8}g_{\rm hyp}$ with constant curvature $-8$.

nodes.name: Weak equivalence via norms of polynomials
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finitely generated group with generating set $\boldsymbol{g}=(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$, and let $\rho_1:\Gamma\to B(H_1)$ and $\rho_2:\Gamma\to B(H_2)$ be unitary representations. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[1.] \itemsep\smallskipamount \item $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ are weakly equivalent. \item $\|P(\rho_1(\boldsymbol{g}),\rho_1(\boldsymbol{g})^*)\|= \|P(\rho_2(\boldsymbol{g}),\rho_2(\boldsymbol{g})^*)\|$ for all $P\in\mathbb{C}\langle x_1,\ldots,x_{2r}\rangle$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.origin_citation: Bekka, de la Harpe & Valette 2008, Thm F.4.4
nodes.label: prop:weakequiv

nodes.name: Sketch of the proof of Song's theorem via strong convergence
nodes.statement: In the present setting, $X$ is the thrice punctured sphere whose fundamental group is $\Gamma\simeq\mathbf{F}_2$. Thus we can define a random representation $\pi_N:\Gamma\to U(N)$ with finite range by choosing $\pi_N(g_1)=U_1^N|_{1^\perp}$ and $\pi_N(g_2)=U_2^N|_{1^\perp}$, where $U_1^N,U_2^N$ are independent random permutation matrices of dimension $N+1$ and we identified $\mathbb{C}^N\simeq \mathbb{C}^{N+1}\cap 1^\perp$. Since Theorem \ref{thm:bc} yields $$ \lim_{N\to\infty} \|P(\pi_N(\boldsymbol{g}),\pi_N(\boldsymbol{g})^*)\| = \|P(\lambda_\Gamma(\boldsymbol{g}),\lambda_\Gamma(\boldsymbol{g})^*)\|, $$ it follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:weakequiv} that the limiting representation $\pi_\infty$ must be weakly equivalent to the regular representation. Thus we obtain a sequence of random minimal surfaces $f_N(X^N)$ in $\mathbb{S}^{2N-1}$ with the desired property.
nodes.statement_short: Random permutation representations of F_2 converge strongly, so the limit representation is weakly equivalent to the regular one and Theorem 5.13 applies.

nodes.name: Define random finite-range representations from permutations
nodes.statement: In the present setting, $X$ is the thrice punctured sphere whose fundamental group is $\Gamma\simeq\mathbf{F}_2$. Thus we can define a random representation $\pi_N:\Gamma\to U(N)$ with finite range by choosing $\pi_N(g_1)=U_1^N|_{1^\perp}$ and $\pi_N(g_2)=U_2^N|_{1^\perp}$, where $U_1^N,U_2^N$ are independent random permutation matrices of dimension $N+1$ and we identified $\mathbb{C}^N\simeq \mathbb{C}^{N+1}\cap 1^\perp$.
nodes.statement_short: Define random finite-range representations from permutations

nodes.name: Strong convergence and Proposition 5.15 give weak equivalence
nodes.statement: Since Theorem \ref{thm:bc} yields $$ \lim_{N\to\infty} \|P(\pi_N(\boldsymbol{g}),\pi_N(\boldsymbol{g})^*)\| = \|P(\lambda_\Gamma(\boldsymbol{g}),\lambda_\Gamma(\boldsymbol{g})^*)\|, $$ it follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:weakequiv} that the limiting representation $\pi_\infty$ must be weakly equivalent to the regular representation.
nodes.statement_short: Strong convergence and Proposition 5.15 give weak equivalence

nodes.name: Obtain the desired minimal surfaces
nodes.statement: Thus we obtain a sequence of random minimal surfaces $f_N(X^N)$ in $\mathbb{S}^{2N-1}$ with the desired property.
nodes.statement_short: Obtain the desired minimal surfaces

nodes.name: Strong convergence for fully residually free groups
nodes.statement: Louder and Magee \cite{LM25} show that there are models of random permutation matrices that strongly converge to the regular representation of any \emph{fully residually free} group: that is, a group that locally embeds in a free group.

nodes.name: Strong convergence for right-angled Artin groups
nodes.statement: Magee and Thomas \cite{MT23} show that there are models of random unitary (but not permutation!)\ matrices that strongly converge to the regular representation of any right-angled Artin group; these are obtained from GUE matrices that act on overlapping factors of a tensor product (see also \cite[\S 9.4]{CGV25}).

nodes.name: Strong convergence of random surface group representations
nodes.statement: Magee, Puder, and the author \cite{MPV25} show that uniformly random permutation representations of the fundamental groups of orientable closed hyperbolic surfaces strongly converge to the regular representation.

nodes.name: Groups without strongly convergent models
nodes.statement: On the other hand, not every discrete group admits a strongly convergent model: there cannot be a model of random permutation matrices that strongly converges to the regular representation of $\mathbf{F}_2\times\mathbf{F}_2\times\mathbf{F}_2$ (a very special case of a right-angled Artin group) \cite[Proposition 2.7]{Mag24}, or a model of random unitary matrices that converges strongly to the regular representation of $\mathrm{SL}_d(\mathbb{Z})$ with $d\ge 4$ \cite{MdlS23}.
nodes.origin_citation: Magee 2024, Prop. 2.7; Magee & de la Salle 2023

nodes.name: Asymptotic expansion for random surface group representations
nodes.statement: For surface groups, one can use the representation theory of $\mathbf{S}_N$ to analyze this model; in particular, this enabled Magee and Puder \cite{MP23} to show that its spectral statistics admit an asymptotic expansion in $\frac{1}{N}$.

nodes.name: Strong convergence for the Gieseking manifold group
nodes.statement: Whether sampling uniformly from the set of permutation matrices $U_1^N,U_2^N$ with $(U_1^N)^2(U_2^N)^2=U_2^NU_1^N$ yields a strongly convergent model is not known.

nodes.name: Random generators and an irreducible representation of S_N
nodes.statement: Let $\boldsymbol{\sigma}=(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)$ be i.i.d.\ uniform random elements of $\mathbf{S}_N$, and let $\pi_N$ be an irreducible representation of $\mathbf{S}_N$.

nodes.name: Strong convergence for all irreducible representations of S_N
nodes.statement: What happens beyond this regime is a mystery: it may even be the case that strong convergence holds for \emph{any} irreducible representations with $\dim(\pi_N)\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Cayley graph of S_N
nodes.statement: Let us recall that the \emph{Cayley graph} $\mathrm{Cay}(\mathbf{S}_N;\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)$ is the graph whose vertex set is $\mathbf{S}_N$, and whose edges are defined by connecting each vertex $\tau$ to its neighbors $\sigma_i\tau$ and $\sigma_i^{-1}\tau$ for $i=1,\ldots,r$.

nodes.name: Optimal spectral gaps of random Cayley graphs of finite groups
nodes.statement: It is a folklore question whether there are sequences of finite groups so that, if generators are chosen independently and uniformly at random, the assocated Cayley graph has an optimal spectral gap. This question is open for any sequence of finite groups.

nodes.name: Irreducibles in the regular representation
nodes.statement: Now recall that every irreducible representation of a finite group is contained in its regular representation with multiplicity equal to its dimension.

nodes.name: Cayley graph norm as supremum over irreducibles
nodes.statement: Thus $$ \|A^N|_{1^\perp}\| = \sup_{\pi_N\ne\mathrm{triv}} \|\pi_N(\sigma_1)+\pi_N(\sigma_1)^* + \cdots + \pi_N(\sigma_r)+\pi_N(\sigma_r)^*\|, $$ where the supremum is over all nontrivial irreducible representations $\pi_N$ (the trivial repesentation is removed by restricting to $1^\perp$).

nodes.name: Sign representation obstructs optimal gaps
nodes.statement: Note that random Cayley graphs of $\mathbf{S}_N$ cannot have an optimal spectral gap with probability $1-o(1)$, as there is a nontrivial $1$-dimensional representation (the sign representation). The latter produces a single eigenvalue that is distributed as twice the sum of $r$ independent Bernoulli variables, which exceeds the lower bound of Lemma \ref{lem:alonboppana} with constant probability.

nodes.name: Optimal spectral gap conjecture for random Cayley graphs of S_N
nodes.statement: Thus we interpret the optimal spectral gap question to mean whether all eigenvalues, except those coming from the trivial and sign representations, meet the lower bound with probability $1-o(1)$. That this is the case is a well known conjecture, see, e.g., \cite[Conjecture~1.6]{RS19}.
also_stated_at: Whether random Cayley graphs of $\mathbf{S}_N$ have an optimal spectral gap is a long-standing question (see section \ref{sec:cayley}) that remains wide open: it has not even been shown that the maximum nontrivial eigenvalue is bounded away from the trivial eigenvalue in this setting.

nodes.name: Kassabov's expanders
nodes.statement: The only known result, due to Kassabov \cite{Kas07}, is that there exists a choice of generators for which the Cayley graph is an expander.

nodes.name: Bourgain-Gamburd expansion and LPS-Margulis Ramanujan Cayley graphs
nodes.statement: In some ways, these groups are considerably better understood than the symmetric group: in this setting, Bourgain and Gamburd \cite{BG08} (see also \cite{Tao15}) show that random Cayley graphs are expanders, while Lubotzky--Phillips--Sarnak \cite{LPS88} and Margulis~\cite{Mar88} provide a determinstic choice of generators for which the Cayley graph has an optimal spectral gap.
nodes.origin_citation: Bourgain & Gamburd 2008; Lubotzky, Phillips & Sarnak 1988; Margulis 1988

nodes.name: Random Cayley graphs with many generators
nodes.statement: The above questions are concerned with random Cayley graphs with a bounded number of generators. If the number of generators is allowed to diverge with the size of the group, rather general results are known: expansion follows from a classical result of Alon and Roichman \cite{AR94}, while optimal spectral gaps were obtained by Brailovskaya and the author in \cite[\S 3.2.3]{BvH24}.

nodes.name: Strong convergence of representations of SU(2)
nodes.statement: The simplest model of this kind arises when $\mathbf{G}=\mathrm{SU}(2)$, which has a single sequence of irreducible representations $ \pi_N = \mathrm{sym}^N V $ where $V$ is the standard representation. The question is then, if $\boldsymbol{U}=(U_1,\ldots,U_r)$ are sampled independently from the Haar measure on $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, whether $\pi_N(\boldsymbol{U})$ strongly converges to the regular representation $\lambda(\boldsymbol{g})$ of the free generators $\boldsymbol{g}=(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$ of $\mathbf{F}_r$.

nodes.name: Weak convergence for representations of compact Lie groups
nodes.statement: For example, if $\boldsymbol{U}=(U_1,\ldots,U_r)$ are sampled independently from the Haar measure on \emph{any} compact connected semisimple Lie group $\mathbf{G}$, and if $\pi_N$ is \emph{any} sequence of irreducible representations of $\mathbf{G}$ with $\dim(\pi_N)\to\infty$, then $\pi_N(\mathbf{G})$ converges weakly to $\lambda(\boldsymbol{g})$; see \cite[Proposition 7.2(1)]{AG25}.

nodes.name: LPS-Margulis Ramanujan Cayley graphs of PSL_2(F_q)
nodes.statement: A potential candidate arises from the celebrated works of Lubotzky--Phillips--Sarnak~\cite{LPS88} and Margulis \cite{Mar88}, who show that the Cayley graph of $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ defined by a certain explicit deterministic choice of generators has an optimal spectral gap.

nodes.name: Voiculescu's question on deterministic strong convergence
nodes.statement: We may therefore ask, by extension, whether the matrices obtained by applying the regular representation of $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ to these generators converge strongly to the regular representation of the free generators of $\mathbf{F}_r$ (cf.\ section \ref{sec:cayley}). This question was raised by Voiculescu \cite[p.\ 146]{Voi93} in an early paper that motivated the development of strong convergence of random matrices by Haagerup and Thorbj{\o}rnsen.

nodes.name: Mobius permutation representation pi_q
nodes.statement: Let $\pi_q\in\mathrm{Hom}(\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z});\mathbf{S}_{q+1})$ be the homomorphism defined by this action, that is, $\pi_q(X)$ is the permutation of the elements of $\mathbf{P}^1(\mathbb{F}_q)$ that maps $z$ to $Xz$.

nodes.name: Buck-Magee conjecture on Mobius permutation models
nodes.statement: The question is whether the permutation matrices $$ (\pi_q(X_1),\ldots,\pi_q(X_r))|_{1^\perp} $$ converge strongly to the regular representation $$ (\lambda_{\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})}(X_1),\ldots,\lambda_{\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})}(X_r)) $$ for any $X_1,\ldots,X_r\in\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$.

nodes.name: Equivalence of the Buck and Magee conjectures
nodes.statement: Note, however, that these two conjectures are actually equivalent by the positivization trick (cf.\ Lemma~\ref{lem:pos} and Remark~\ref{rem:posnonfree}) since $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ satisfies the rapid decay and unique trace properties \cite{Cha17,BCD94}.

nodes.name: Optimal spectral gap
nodes.statement: In this survey, we have said that a sequence of graphs has an \emph{optimal spectral gap} if satisfies this bound in reverse, that is, if $$ \|A^N|_{1^\perp}\| \le 2\sqrt{d-1} + o(1). $$

nodes.name: Ramanujan graph
nodes.statement: However, a more precise question that has attracted significant attention in the literature is whether it is possible for graphs to have their nontrivial eigenvalues be \emph{strictly} bounded by the spectral radius of the universal cover, without an error term: that is, can one have $d$-regular graphs with $N$ vertices such that $$ \|A^N|_{1^\perp}\| \le 2\sqrt{d-1} $$ for arbitrarily large $N$? Graphs satisfying this property are called \emph{Ramanujan graphs}.

nodes.name: Existence of Ramanujan graphs
nodes.statement: Ramanujan graphs do indeed exist and can be obtained by several remarkable constructions; we refer to the breakthrough papers \cite{LPS88,Mar88,MSS15,HMY25}.
nodes.origin_citation: Lubotzky, Phillips & Sarnak 1988; Margulis 1988; Marcus, Spielman & Srivastava 2015; Huang, McKenzie & Yau 2025

nodes.name: Ramanujan form of strong convergence
nodes.statement: For example, one may ask whether there exist $N\times N$ permutation matrices $\boldsymbol{U}^N=(U_1^N,\ldots,U_r^N)$ so that \begin{equation} \|P(\boldsymbol{U}^N,\boldsymbol{U}^{N*})|_{1^\perp}\| \le \|P(\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{u}^*)\| \end{equation} for every polynomial $P$, where $\boldsymbol{u}$ are as defined in Theorem \ref{thm:bc}.

nodes.name: Ramanujan-type strong convergence inequality
nodes.statement: \|P(\boldsymbol{U}^N,\boldsymbol{U}^{N*})|_{1^\perp}\| \le \|P(\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{u}^*)\|
nodes.label: eq:ramanotjan

nodes.name: No exact Ramanujan strong convergence in fixed dimension
nodes.statement: It cannot be the case that \eqref{eq:ramanotjan} holds simultaneously for all $P$ in fixed dimension $N$, since that would imply by Lemma \ref{lem:upperlower} that $C^*_{\rm red}(\mathbf{F}_r)$ embeds in $\mathrm{M}_N(\mathbb{C})$.

nodes.name: Weak Ramanujan form of strong convergence
nodes.statement: A weaker form of this question is whether for each $P$, there exist $\boldsymbol{U}^N$ (which may now depend on $P$) for arbitrarily large $N$ so that \eqref{eq:ramanotjan} holds.

nodes.name: Ramanujan property and the Ihara zeta function
nodes.statement: The interest in Ramanujan graphs stems in part from an analogy with number theory: the Ramanujan property of a graph is equivalent to the validity of the Riemann hypothesis for its Ihara zeta function \cite[Theorem 7.4]{Ter11}.

nodes.name: Ramanujan surfaces and the Selberg zeta function
nodes.statement: In the setting of hyperbolic surfaces, the analogous ``Ramanujan property'' that a hyperbolic surface $X$ has $\lambda_1(X)\ge\frac{1}{4}$ is equivalent to the validity of the Riemann hypothesis for its Selberg zeta function \cite[\S 6]{Mur87}.

nodes.name: Selberg eigenvalue conjecture
nodes.statement: An important conjecture of Selberg \cite{Sar95} predicts that a specific family of hyperbolic surfaces has this property.

nodes.name: Optimal dimension of matrix coefficients
nodes.statement: While only the case $D_N=N$ is needed for that purpose, the optimal range of $D_N$ for which strong convergence holds remains open: for both Gaussian and Haar distributed matrices, it is known that strong convergence holds when $D_N=e^{o(N)}$ and can fail when $D_N\ge e^{CN^2}$ \cite{CGV25}.
nodes.section: 6.6 The optimal dimension of matrix coefficients

nodes.name: Tracy-Widom edge statistics for random regular graphs
nodes.statement: In a major breakthrough, Huang--McKenzie--Yau \cite{HMY25} recently showed that the largest nontrivial eigenvalue of a random regular graph has the same behavior, which implies the remarkable result that about $69\%$ of random regular graphs are Ramanujan.

nodes.name: Optimal fluctuation scale in strong convergence
nodes.statement: It is natural to expect that except in degenerate situations, the same scale and edge statistics should arise in strong convergence problems.

nodes.name: Optimal fluctuations for quadratic polynomials of Wigner matrices
nodes.statement: However, to date the optimal scale of fluctuations $N^{-2/3}$ has only been established for the norm of quadratic polynomials of Wigner matrices \cite{FKN24}.

nodes.name: Male's theorem on random and deterministic matrices
nodes.statement: Let $\boldsymbol{G}^N=(G_1^N,\ldots,G_r^N)$ be i.i.d.\ GUE matrices, and let $\boldsymbol{B}^N=(B_1^N,\ldots,B_s^N)$ be deterministic matrices of the same dimension. It was realized by Male \cite{Mal12} that the Haagerup--Thorbj{\o}rnsen theorem admits the following extension: if it is assumed that $\boldsymbol{B}^N$ converges strongly to some limiting family of operators $\boldsymbol{b}$, then $(\boldsymbol{G}^N,\boldsymbol{B}^N)$ converges strongly to $(\boldsymbol{s},\boldsymbol{b})$ where the free semicircular family $\boldsymbol{s}$ is taken to be freely independent of $\boldsymbol{b}$ in the sense of Voiculescu.

nodes.name: Joint strong convergence for Haar unitaries and deterministic matrices
nodes.statement: This joint strong convergence property of random and deterministic matrices was extended to Haar unitaries by Collins and Male \cite{CM14}, and was developed in a nonasymptotic form by Collins, Guionnet, and Parraud \cite{CGP22,Par21,Par23,Par23b}.
nodes.origin_citation: Collins & Male 2014; Collins, Guionnet & Parraud 2022; Parraud

nodes.name: Joint strong convergence of permutations and deterministic matrices
nodes.statement: Thus a counterpart of this form of strong convergence for random permutation matrices remains open.

nodes.name: Brown measure
nodes.statement: The natural object of this kind, whose definition reduces to the complex eigenvalue distribution in the case of matrices, is called the \emph{Brown measure} \cite[Chapter~11]{MS17}.

nodes.name: Convergence of complex eigenvalues under strong convergence
nodes.statement: It is tempting to conjecture that if a family of random matrices $\boldsymbol{X}^N$ strongly converges to a family of limiting operators $\boldsymbol{x}$, then the empirical distribution of the complex eigenvalues of any noncommutative polynomial $P(\boldsymbol{X}^N,\boldsymbol{X}^{N*})$ should converge to $P(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{x}^*)$.

nodes.name: Complex eigenvalues of quadratic polynomials of Ginibre matrices
nodes.statement: To date, this has only been proved in the special case of quadratic polynomials of independent complex Ginibre matrices \cite{CGH22}.

nodes.name: Intrinsic freeness for complex eigenvalues
nodes.statement: One may similarly ask whether the intrinsic freeness principle extends to complex eigenvalues of non-self-adjoint random matrices. For example, is there a counterpart of Theorem \ref{thm:intrfree} for complex eigenvalues, and if so what are the objects that should appear in it?
